facts.statement: The Lantern telescope has a 2.4 metre primary mirror.
The Lantern telescope sits at 3,180 metres on Mount Aubrel.
Observing time on the Lantern telescope is allocated every April by the Tern committee.
The Lantern dome closes automatically when wind exceeds 15 metres per second.
The Brine archive keeps raw exposures for twelve years before deleting them.
Brine stores calibrated images in Zarr format on a Ceph cluster.
Researchers request Brine data through the Sounding web portal.
Brine replicates every night to a tape library in Orkney Hall.
Quillfeather removes cosmic-ray hits with a median stack of five frames.
Quillfeather is written in Julia and scheduled with Airflow.
A Quillfeather nightly run takes about three hours on 64 cores.
Quillfeather flags any frame whose seeing is worse than 1.8 arcseconds.
The Thistle arm has six joints and lifts at most 4 kilograms.
Thistle's gripper uses a vacuum cup for flat parts and fingers for the rest.
A Thistle arm must be recalibrated after every 400 hours of operation.
Thistle stops within 30 milliseconds when its light curtain is broken.
Gossamer firmware runs on an RP2040 microcontroller.
Gossamer updates are signed with Ed25519 keys held by the release team.
Gossamer rolls back to the previous image if the new one fails to boot three times.
Gossamer talks to the controller over CAN bus at 500 kbit/s.
The Larkspur build farm has 40 runners managed by Buildkite.
Larkspur caches compiled objects in an sccache bucket for fourteen days.
A Larkspur job that runs longer than 90 minutes is cancelled.
Larkspur runners are reimaged from a golden image every Sunday night.
Cobble is a garbage-collected language that compiles to WebAssembly.
Cobble modules are fetched by the tool named trowel.
Cobble reports a type error when a match expression misses a case.
Cobble strings are immutable UTF-8 byte sequences.
